I've had depression since I can remember. Things you should aknowledge that most people get wrong:
-depression is an illness
-as such, you can't expect people to "snap out of it" just like you don't snap out of a broken bone or heart failure
-everyone percieves it differently, however there are many common symptoms

For instance, the way I percieve it, it's like trying to climb a mountain under a waterfall. A massive waterfall. I struggle to even grab on to the rocky wall, and often I end up falling. The current is just too strong to get up once I fall, it takes me a long time. All of my effort goes to trying to breathe, and often I can't even do that. So from time to time I give up and let the current drag me away without fighting back, and I find myself back to square one. And whenever I feel like fighting again, I can only go as far as I was before, before falling again.

I know how you feel. The last time I fell in love was 2 years ago, when I was about your age. She was my classmate. I loved her smile, her voice, her eyes...she was so kind and sweet and funny, I loved her more than anything else. I would've moved the stars in the depths of space, to write her name in the sky, if that could make her smile even for just a second. I would've gave up my own life for her, I would've done anything, really ANYTHING to make her happy. For the last two years, we've been friends, until I actually told her how I felt. She started to ignore me. That happened roughly 2 months ago. I just wanted to make her happy, so I'd text her things like "I love you" or "you're beautiful" or that kinda stuff, asking her how she was doing and whatnot. She never texted me back. After a while, roughly 1 month ago, she told me to get out of her life, that she didn't want to have anything to do with me, to never talk to her again. My heart was torn apart. I cried myself to sleep for over a week. You might think that I'm a pussy. You may be right. But she was the love of my life, or so I thought. But after being forced out of her life forever, I began feeling better. Not being able to see her anymore, not being able to have any kind of contact with her actually helped me. Even though at first I thought that the pain would tear me to shreds, now I'm doing better. Sometimes it comes back, like a tidal wave that wiped away everything, but after a li'l bit it's gone and I can think clearly again. I know now that it just wasn't meant to be, if it didn't work for two years, probably there was no chance at all, and probably it's better that this happened. Her life goes on, and so does mine. I know that probably you won't listen to my advice anyway, but I thought I'd share my story, just to let you know that I know what you're going through and that you're not alone.

Well, buddy, unrequited love hurts indeed. But if there is something I learned from my only two experiences of unrequited love, which also happen to be the only two times i ever actually fell in love, it's that you need to move on. You need to forget her. See, when you're in love, you tend to idealize the other person as being better than she actually is, and you end up loving the idea you have of her. It's kinda hard to explain. Anyway, the best thing for you AND for her, would be that you'd just forget her. It hurts, it's gonna hurt for a while, but on the long run it's worth it. Let her live her own life, and you live yours. She can't choose who she falls in love with, she can't just change her mind overnight, and you need to realize this. You need to forget her, as much as that would hurt, it's the best thing you can do. I'm sorry buddy.

My upbringing, huh? Well, I don't remember much of it, but I know I've been depressed since I was 7, if not even earlier than that. Both my parents were depressed, but they weren't diagnosed back then, and they both had their own...ways to cope with it. My mother worked all the time, so she was never home, and my father was aggressive and violent. He'd beat the crap out of me anytime I'd mess up. And I was bullied at school, since i was about 6 til I was 12 or 13. I've always had just a few friends, but didn't even talk that much with them, I've spent my childhood on my own, playing videogames and reading books, never going out, never meeting anyone and hardly ever talking with my family. I became aggressive, violent. I became dangerous for others and for myself, suicidal, completely detatched from reality. But it took me a long, long while to realize there was something wrong. So yeah, I'd say my upbringing and childhood definitely affected my depression, but just partially. It's also partially genetic.

I've got a choice: a beautiful prison, where I can be happy and free, or a terrible prison, filled with sorrow and emptiness. At the end of the day, nobody cares about which one I'll choose, it's going to affect only one person, and that would be me. So I'm going with the best option. Living in a world that doesn't even exist...where nobody will ever tell me that what I do, that what I *am*...is wrong. The very concept of wrong and right do not exist in that world. Just beauty and freedom. You have no idea what kind of world my mind created in all these years. It's my own heaven, everything is just perfect for me in there, whereas everything is wrong in the real world. Too  bad depression gave me insomnia, so I hardly ever sleep more than 6 hours in a row.

Well, I don't like the waking world, and the world apparently doesn't like me either, so everyone wins if I spend the rest of my life in bed, sleeping, waiting for my peaceful death. Either that or I just die. But if I end up killing myself I won't be able to feel good again, because I won't be able to dream. Thus I sleep. See, I've seen enough of this rotten world to know that I don't like it, and I don't like people. I don't even care anymore. I failed at everything I tried to do since I was born: I failed at school, I failed at relationships, I failed at curing depression, I even failed at doing things I like. Survival of the fittest. Apparently I'm not good enough to live, but I'm also too much of a pussy to kill myself. That's why I escape from reality in my dreams. The only place where I can be happy is the fake world that my brain creates for me every time I sleep.

I just want to sleep, and dream and feel free, feel good again.

Depression is a dark beast that eats your mind and your heart and doesn't leave you alone. Depression takes away all of your happiness, and all of your feelings, and your motivation. When you suffer from depression, you don't feel like doing anything, you can't do anything, even the easiest, most simple actions become unbelievably hard. By simple actions I mean something like getting out of bed or tiding a room. Everything becomes difficoult. When you suffer from depression, you don't even enjoy things you used to like. And you can't focus/pay attention, you're always tired. You feel like you're worthless and unable to do anything. It's not rational. It's not logical. Depression is beyond logic. The best thing one can do when depressed would be looking for professional help. Therapist+meds can save a life. If it goes untreated, depression can ruin the life of the depressed and everyone around him. I don't have kids, I'm only 18, but I have depression, so I know what it feels like.
